title: pool_release: open() on release path adds a syscall to every operation completion
description: crypto2dev_pool_release() calls open(CRYPTO2DEV_PATH, O_RDWR|O_CLOEXEC) to pre-open a fresh fd for the next caller. This means every cipher/hash operation completion incurs one extra open() syscall. Alternative: do not pre-open; let acquire() open on demand (recovery_slot path already handles this). The pre-open amortizes open() latency from the acquire critical path to the release path, which is correct for hide-latency scenarios. However, for steady-state TLS where every encrypt is followed by a decrypt before the slot is reused, the fd returned from release is immediately re-acquired by the next operation — the pre-open is wasted. The benefit only appears when multiple threads compete for pool slots. For single-threaded use (common in embedded), the pre-open is pure overhead.
